Let’s talk about Chapter 7: Practical Steps Toward a Radical Life.
Big ideas can spark something inside us, can’t they? But when it comes to actually living them out, it’s easy to feel a bit lost—almost like you’re standing on the shore, staring out at this endless ocean, and you’re not quite sure how to take that first step into the waves.
Here’s a comforting truth: real change hardly ever happens overnight. Instead, it’s born out of small, thoughtful choices—one after another, day by day.
There’s a story about a young woman who started feeling this gentle tug on her heart after reading stories of people who made big sacrifices and served others. At first, she didn’t have a clue where to begin. She wasn’t being asked to move to another country or give away everything she owned. So, she just looked at her regular, everyday life.
What did she do? She began by setting aside a bit of her income for causes she cared about. She volunteered at a local shelter. She even started inviting her neighbors over for dinner. Every step seemed small—almost like it might not even matter. But as the days went by, her habits slowly shifted, and something in her heart changed too.
Most of us don’t realize just how much our routines shape who we are. Living out radical faith isn’t really about huge, dramatic gestures. It’s about tweaking those daily choices—rethinking how you spend your money, where you put your time, and who you invest in. Sometimes, it means simplifying your life or letting go of things that just aren’t that important. Other times, it’s about investing in people rather than chasing after more stuff.
The book lays out plenty of practical ideas, but it keeps reminding us that there’s no formula—no one-size-fits-all answer. Maybe your next step is to learn about needs around the world, to pray for people in tough situations, or to support someone who’s out there serving. For you, it might look like opening your home, reaching out to forgive someone, or choosing to stand up for people who can’t speak for themselves.
What becomes really clear is this: the path to radical faith is made up of countless small decisions. Each one is a chance to trust a little more, to give a bit more, and to love a whole lot deeper. The goal isn’t to be perfect. It’s simply to keep moving forward—one honest, intentional step at a time.
